text.title: CDN-Fronted Static Deploy — Decision Tree
text.summary: First gate: is there a caching proxy between the origin and the user that this pipeline cannot purge? Everything below follows from the answer, and each leaf names the rule that applies.

decision-tree.root-question: Does a caching proxy sit in front of the origin, and does the deploy pipeline lack credentials to purge it?

conclusion.verdict: Skip. Invalidate at the edge on deploy. Content-hashing URLs is still good hygiene but it is no longer load-bearing, and the report artefact has nothing to prove.

STOP before anything else. If the HTML is edge-cached, hashing the URLs inside it cannot reach a browser. Get the HTML uncached — origin cache-control, a bypass rule — or get purge credentials. There is no build-side fix.
Stamp every asset URL with its own content hash as the last build step, and add the same check to CI in report-only mode. This is the whole lever; everything else defends it.
Register `/sw.js?v=<hash>`, hashed over the worker source plus the precache file list. Never over the files' contents — the pages carry the value, so content hashing is circular.
Split the match: exact for `/assets/*` carrying `?v=`, `ignoreSearch` for unversioned paths. Left global, it silently cancels the hash fix for every client the worker controls.
Make navigations network-first with a cache fallback. Stale documents pin stale hashed assets, so a document-level staleness bug presents as a whole release failing to appear.
Invert it: `--include` per shipped path then `--exclude='*'`, keeping `--delete` and deliberately not `--delete-excluded`. Orphan removal becomes a separate step naming one file at a time.
Set `fetch-depth: 0`. Symptom to recognise: the step passes on every developer machine and fails only on the runner.
Send a curl-like User-Agent before debugging the deploy. Bot protection rejecting a default library User-Agent looks identical to a broken release.
Add the stamp check to CI as a failing gate, kept separate from any full re-render check so it stays deterministic on a runner whose toolchain differs from the author's.
Emit the edge-freshness report and probe the live URL. A green pipeline is not the evidence; the recorded edge response is.

example.trace: static site, proxy in front, HTML DYNAMIC, assets immutable and unstamped -> r1-content-hash-the-url
